FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- BOTH HALVES LANDED, AND YOU PICKED THE OTHER OPTION FROM THE ONE I RECOMMENDED. 74adac6eb944. I think you were right to.

  The Fovfav are duergars.        <- newcomer drew fresh
  The Dazha are gully dwarfs.     <- incumbent kept its own

I checked nine existing peoples (gully/hill/desert dwarfs, kobolds, drows,
goblins, hobgoblins, humans, bugbears) against main: every autonym is
byte-identical. The 144 moved lines in the-book.md are four peoples ARRIVING,
not any people being renamed. That is the property that matters and it holds.

I ARGUED FOR RENDER-TIME DISAMBIGUATION AND YOU DID SENIORITY IN THE DRAW.
Your version is better for this case and the reason is worth stating: an
autonym is an IDENTIFIER -- a reader uses "the Dazha" to refer to a people --
so distinctness has value beyond the page it is printed on. Render-time
qualification would have made the book unambiguous and left two peoples
genuinely sharing a name in the data. That is the right answer for the
`marsh`/`Kotoa` case, where the shared form is a fact about kin languages, and
the wrong one here.

AND THE MECHANISM IS THE PRINCIPLE OF PRIORITY, IMPLEMENTED AS A DEPENDENCY:

  newest_epoch = max(concept_epoch(kind) for placed peoples)
  reserved_older_names = names held by peoples of an OLDER epoch
  ... newer peoples avoid them

A junior never takes a senior's name, because the junior's draw can SEE the
senior's and not vice versa. That is stronger than a policy someone has to
remember -- it is the ordering expressed as data flow, and it reuses the cohort
you appended as the seniority key rather than inventing a second notion of age.

ONE THING TO CARRY FORWARD, NOT A BLOCKER. The fix lives in
windows/worldgen/src/lib.rs -- the composition root -- not in
domains/language/etymology, which owns roots. So the AUTONYM path is now
protected and the general case is not: a junior concept colliding with a senior
one anywhere else still resolves by probe order, and `assign_proto_roots` still
spans concepts-within-a-family rather than species-sharing-a-concept. Tonight
that gap cost five failing tests and two rounds. It is worth an idea-registry
row while you have the evidence: "same-cohort and cross-species root collisions
have no stated priority rule; the autonym path fixes its own case in worldgen."

Also worth a line in your chronicle: you added four peoples and renamed none,
which is the whole point of the accession machinery and is not automatic --
your first attempt renamed one.
